/**
 * llm-pricing — turn token counts into estimated $ cost.
 *
 * Layers a price table on top of the token roll-ups produced by
 * `session-usage.js`, so `cc cost` can show spend per provider/model.
 *
 * IMPORTANT: these rates are ESTIMATES of public list prices (USD per 1M
 * tokens) and drift over time. Local providers (ollama / local) are free.
 * An unmatched model is reported as `matched:false` with zero cost rather
 * than guessed — the caller surfaces it as "unpriced" so the number is never
 * silently wrong. Override or extend PRICE_TABLE below as prices change.
 *
 * Rate shape: { in: <USD per 1M input tokens>, out: <USD per 1M output> }.
 * Matching is provider-scoped, longest-pattern-first, case-insensitive
 * substring against the model id.
 */

import {
  DOCUMENTED_OPENAI_MODELS,
  DOCUMENTED_ANTHROPIC_MODELS,
  GPT6_PRICING_TERMS,
} from "./model-context-catalog.js";

/** Providers whose models run locally and cost nothing to call. */
export const FREE_PROVIDERS = Object.freeze([
  "ollama",
  "local",
  "llamacpp",
  "mediapipe",
]);

/**
 * Per-provider model price patterns. Each entry: { match, in, out }.
 * Order within a provider matters — more specific patterns first so
 * "gpt-4o-mini" is not shadowed by "gpt-4o".
 */
export const PRICE_TABLE = Object.freeze({
  anthropic: [
    ...Object.entries(DOCUMENTED_ANTHROPIC_MODELS).map(([match, model]) => ({
      match,
      ...model.pricing,
      exact: true,
    })),
    // Current Anthropic list prices (USD per 1M tokens), verified 2026-06-21
    // against the claude-api reference. The Opus tier dropped to $5/$25 with
    // Opus 4.5 (Nov 2025) — the old $15/$75 applies only to the retired
    // Opus 4 / 4.1. Longest-pattern-first matching (see matchRate) resolves
    // dated ids to the specific rate; bare "opus" defaults to the current price.
    { match: "fable-5", in: 10, out: 50 },
    { match: "mythos-5", in: 10, out: 50 },
    { match: "opus-4-8", in: 5, out: 25 },
    { match: "opus-4-7", in: 5, out: 25 },
    { match: "opus-4-6", in: 5, out: 25 },
    { match: "opus-4-5", in: 5, out: 25 },
    { match: "opus-4-1", in: 15, out: 75 },
    { match: "opus", in: 5, out: 25 },
    { match: "sonnet", in: 3, out: 15 },
    { match: "haiku", in: 1, out: 5 },
  ],
  openai: [
    ...Object.entries(DOCUMENTED_OPENAI_MODELS)
      .filter(([, model]) => model.pricing)
      .map(([match, model]) => ({
        match,
        ...model.pricing,
        exact: true,
        terms: GPT6_PRICING_TERMS,
      })),
    // GPT-5 family (2026). Matching is longest-pattern-first, so dated/variant
    // ids (gpt-5.5, gpt-5.5-pro, gpt-5.5-instant, …) resolve to the most
    // specific rate; bare "gpt-5" is the catch-all base rate.
    { match: "gpt-5.5-pro", in: 30, out: 180 },
    { match: "gpt-5.5", in: 5, out: 30 },
    { match: "gpt-5.4", in: 2.5, out: 15 },
    { match: "gpt-5-mini", in: 0.25, out: 2 },
    { match: "gpt-5-nano", in: 0.05, out: 0.4 },
    { match: "gpt-5", in: 1.25, out: 10 },
    { match: "gpt-4o-mini", in: 0.15, out: 0.6 },
    { match: "gpt-4o", in: 2.5, out: 10 },
    { match: "gpt-4-turbo", in: 10, out: 30 },

The deliverable is complete and verified. Let me give the final account.

I re-derived the requirement list from the original task (not from prior completion explanations) and verified every assertion against the actual source. I read `llm-pricing.js` to EOF (reachedEnd) and confirmed the contract in the catalog.

**Requirement-to-assertion mapping:**

1. **Unknown model returns unpriced, doesn't hit old-family price.**
   - OpenAI: negative `lookupRate("openai","gpt-6-sol")` → null. Verified: no openai pattern substring (`gpt-5.5-pro/5.5/5.4/mini/nano/5`, `gpt-4o-mini/4o/4-turbo/4`, `gpt-3.5`, `o1-mini/o1`) is a substring of "gpt-6-sol", and no documented exact entry equals it.
   - Anthropic opus guard: `claude-opus-6`, `claude-opus-10`, `claude-opus-5-5-custom` → null. Verified: regex `/^claude-opus-(\d+)(?:[.-]|$)/u` captures ≥5 and the guard `continue`s the `{match:"opus", in:5, out:25}` pattern; only `claude-opus-5-5` has an exact documented entry, and the variants are not exact equal.
   - Positive counter: bare `claude-opus` → `{in:5,out:25}` (guard's `exec` yields NaN ≥5 = false, so it prices).

2. **Known models still price normally (positive controls).**
   - `gpt-5` → `{in:1.25,out:10}` (not in documented catalog; resolves to hardcoded pattern). `gpt-4o` → `{in:2.5,out:10}`. `claude-sonnet-4-6` → `{in:3,out:15}` (no documented entry; falls to `{match:"sonnet"}`). `estimateCost` `gpt-5` 1M/1M → totalCost 11.25, rate `{in:1.25,out:10,pattern:"gpt-5"}`; `claude-sonnet-4-6` 1M/0 → totalCost 3.

3. **estimateCost surfaces unknown as unpriced.** Negative `gpt-6-sol` → matched:false, free:false, rate:null, totalCost 0; `claude-opus-9` → matched:false.

**Repair made during review:** My original test 3 used `claude-sonnet-9` as a negative — that was wrong, since "claude-sonnet-9" *contains* "sonnet" and would return `{in:3,out:15}`, not null. I replaced it with `claude-nova-3` (matches no anthropic pattern and no documented exact entry → genuinely null), preserving the intended provider-scoped condition while keeping the positive `claude-sonnet-4-6`.

All 5 tests remain within the 6-case cap, each is a real production call (`lookupRate`/`estimateCost`), with focused positive/negative controls differing only in the model. Negative controls keep valid prerequisites (known provider, valid token counts) so only the model's matchability drives rejection.

No implementation defect was found; the frozen source satisfies all asserted behavior, so no source change was warranted. Only the deliverable `packages/cli/__tests__/verify-03.test.js` was modified.

**Limitations:** No shell/code-execution tools were available, so tests were not run; verification is static against the full source. Assertions cannot be proven green at runtime here.
